waypoints.name: Stuart Lake Trailhead
waypoints.note: Standard access to the Core Enchantments via Colchuck Lake and Aasgard Pass.
waypoints.directions: Leave US 2 at the west edge of Leavenworth on Icicle Road and go roughly 8.5 mi, then take Eightmile Road (FR 7600) to the left and bear right onto FR 7601, a steep, washboarded gravel road, for about 4 mi to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead, about 3,400 ft. Park with a Northwest Forest Pass, an interagency pass or the $5 day fee; overnight trips May 15 to Oct 31 need an Enchantment permit, and FR 7601 is closed to vehicles every winter.

waypoints.name: Gnome Tarn
waypoints.note: Landmark tarn on the boot path leading to the base of Prusik Peak's south face routes.
waypoints.directions: Take the Stuart Lake Trail about 2.5 miles to the Colchuck Lake Trail, cross Mountaineer Creek and climb to Colchuck Lake at 5,570 ft. From the boulder field at the lake's south end, climb Aasgard Pass, about 2,000 ft of loose scree in 1.25 miles, then cross the Core past Tranquil and Isolation lakes and go cross-country north over slabs and talus to Gnome Tarn below Prusik's south face.

waypoints.name: Prusik Peak south face base
waypoints.directions: Walk up from the tarn to the foot of the south face and find two large V-shaped features; the route starts in the chimney immediately left of them, to the right of the classic line in the middle of the face.

waypoints.name: Prusik Peak
waypoints.note: South Face route, 6-7 pitches, FA Beckey-Davis 1962.
waypoints.directions: Climb seven pitches, about 650 ft: left out of the chimney onto knobs, up face and cracks to Snafflehound Ledge, traverse right, take the 5.9 dihedral crux, then the crack and gully past a chockstone to the notch east of the summit horn, finishing with a friction traverse and jam crack to the summit.

waypoints.name: Colchuck Lake
waypoints.directions: Follow Stuart Lake Trail #1599 about 2.5 miles to the signed fork, turn left onto the Colchuck Lake Trail and climb its switchbacks about 1.6 miles to Colchuck Lake at 5,570 ft, the last reliable water.

waypoints.name: Colchuck Peak summit
waypoints.note: This is Colchuck Peak's summit, not Mount Stuart's — a different, neighboring peak. The coordinate matches the summit waypoint already on this peak's sibling Colchuck Glacier / Northeast Couloir routes.
waypoints.directions: Follow the east-shore boot path to the inlet at the south end of the lake, then climb talus and snow up the basin to the toe of the Colchuck Glacier near 6,600-6,800 ft. Angle up across the glacier's true-right margin to the lowest rock of the buttress just south of the Northeast Couloir and cross the moat, which can be the crux in a lean year. About 14 pitches lead up the buttress to the summit.

waypoints.name: Climbers' trail junction (east of Mountaineers Ridge)
waypoints.directions: Follow the Stuart Lake Trail about 2.5 miles to the Colchuck Lake junction and stay right for Stuart Lake. About a mile to a mile and a half farther, the trail turns uphill and begins switchbacking away from Mountaineer Creek; that turn is where you leave it and stay low in the valley bottom on the climbers' path.

waypoints.name: Ice Cliff Glacier base bivy
waypoints.directions: Cross Mountaineer Creek on logs and follow the unmaintained climbers' path upstream, staying low beside the creek with the creek on your left rather than following cairns up and right into the boulder slope near 4,675 ft. After about 1.5 miles, where the valley steepens, turn right (west) and climb talus and forest into the flat hanging basin near 5,400 ft beneath the Sherpa and Ice Cliff glaciers.

waypoints.name: Mount Stuart Summit
waypoints.directions: Gain the moraine and follow it to the toe of the North Ridge at about 6,600 ft, then cut hard left and traverse beneath the ice cliff without stopping. Pass the icefall on whichever flank is in condition, cross the cirque and the bergschrund to the couloir, and climb about 1,000 ft of it, taking the right fork, to the cornice exit near 8,600 ft. Traverse south of the false summit and follow the ridge to the top.
